title: Projective constructibility from projective-line constructibility
statement:
Suppose $\mathcal C(\mathbf P^1_T\to T)$ holds for every
finite-type $k$-scheme $T$. Then $\mathcal C(f)$ holds for
every projective morphism $f:X\to S$ between finite-type
$k$-schemes, using the conventions of
[def-finrepair-property-c], [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions].
Here projective has the closed-embedding convention of [def-pc-projective-morphism].

proof.text: Use the existing recursive schemes Z_m = ProjectiveSpace.projectiveLinePow m S, with Z_0 = S and Z_(m+1) = P^1_(Z_m), and projections p_m = projectiveLinePowProj m S. The projective-space projections are proper by [lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-proper], hence locally of finite type and quasi-compact. Induction and composition give both finite-type conditions for p_m followed by the structure morphism S to Spec(k). Equip Z_m with exactly this structure morphism. The coefficient convention pulls back along any scheme morphism: a unit N in global sections maps to the same natural-number cast under the map on global sections; positivity, finiteness of Lambda and annihilation are unchanged.

source.place: Second paragraph: the successive finite-type bases

proof.text: For any closed immersion j:A to B in the domain of C, the finite-type structure on B makes B locally Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. Thus the open complement of j is quasi-compact. Use the existing quasi-compact-complement wrapper of [lem-fin-closed-immersion] to preserve source-library constructibility under j_*. Convert between source-library constructibility and finite-constant-value constructibility by [lem-weil-pbc-constructible-etale-module-sheaf-comparison]. The closed immersion is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-finite], so [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-direct-image-exact] gives exactness. The existing bounded-below comparison rightDerivedFunctorPlusIsoMapDerivedCategoryPlus and mapDerivedCategoryPlusSingleFunctor identify Rj_*(F[0]) with (j_*F)[0]. Taking homology gives constructibility in degree zero and zero in positive degrees. The zero sheaf is constructible using the trivial stratification (the existing IsConstructibleSheaf.of_isZero). Consequently C(j) holds. This is proved in the private Lean helper constructibleHigherDirectImages_closed; no intermediate hole is introduced.

source.place: Last paragraph: exact constructibility-preserving closed pushforward; also the identity base case

proof.text: Prove C(p_m) by induction on m. For m = 0 the projection is the identity, which is a closed immersion, so the preceding step applies. For m+1 the first projection Z_(m+1) to Z_m satisfies C by the projective-line hypothesis with the pulled-back coefficient convention and the finite-type instances of step 1. Compose it with p_m using [lem-finrepair-composition-c]. This supplies C for every projective-line tower projection over S.

source.place: Second paragraph: composition of projective-line projections; the n=0 sentence

proof.text: Choose the finite coordinate type I and global closed embedding i:X to P(I;S) from [def-pc-projective-morphism]. Projective space is finite type over k by properness of its projection followed by the given structure of S, and its coefficient convention is pulled back from S. If I is empty, P(I;S) is empty (ProjectiveSpace.instIsEmpty), so its projection to S is a closed immersion and step 2 gives C. If I is nonempty, use ProjectiveSpace.exists_isFinite_surjective_projectiveLinePow, recorded with [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-product-finite], together with [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-product-surjective]: there are m and a finite surjective sigma:Z_m to P(I;S) whose composite with the projective projection is p_m. This source-library theorem handles every finite nonempty coordinate type, including the single-coordinate, dimension-zero case, and needs no Noetherian-base hypothesis. Rewrite the composite using its over-base equation and apply [lem-finrepair-finite-surjection-cancellation] to step 3. This proves C for the projective-space projection.

source.place: First paragraph: projective embedding; second paragraph: symmetric-product cover and finite-surjection cancellation

proof.text: Step 2 gives C(i) for the chosen closed immersion. Compose it with C for the projective-space projection from step 4 using [lem-finrepair-composition-c]. The factorization equation identifies this composite with the original f, proving precisely the unchanged theorem statement.

source.place: Last paragraph: composition with the closed embedding

proof_origin.place: Proof implemented by V2 using the existing source-library recursive symmetric-product cover; closed immersion and coefficient transport proved as private helpers.
